title: Gut Microbiota and Trimethylamine N-Oxide in Cardiovascular Disease
abstract: The intestinal microbiome metabolizes dietary phosphatidylcholine and L-carnitine into trimethylamine, which is subsequently oxidized in the liver to trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO). Elevated circulating TMAO levels have been correlated with enhanced atherosclerosis, platelet hyperreactivity, and increased risk of major adverse cardiovascular events.

title: Short-Chain Fatty Acids as Regulators of Blood Pressure
abstract: Bacterial fermentation of dietary non-digestible carbohydrates yields short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), notably acetate, propionate, and butyrate. These metabolites modulate host blood pressure through interactions with olfactory receptors and G-protein coupled receptors in the vascular endothelium.

title: The Intestinal Barrier and Systemic Inflammation in Heart Failure
abstract: Patients diagnosed with chronic heart failure frequently demonstrate compromised gut barrier integrity, termed leaky gut syndrome. Bacterial translocation and circulating lipopolysaccharides trigger systemic inflammatory cascades and worsen cardiomyopathy outcomes.

title: Dietary Fiber and Microbiome Diversity: Impacts on Atherosclerosis
abstract: A high-fiber nutritional intervention induces marked shifts in microbial taxonomic diversity and abundance of short-chain fatty acid producers. This is accompanied by reductions in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and decreased arterial plaque deposition.

title: Probiotics and Gut-Heart Metabolic Crosstalk
abstract: Administration of specific Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium strains alters bile acid deconjugation and reduces hepatic lipid accumulation, offering novel therapeutic avenues for hyperlipidemia and cardiovascular comorbidities.

title: Metabolomic Profiling of Gut Dysbiosis in Ischemic Heart Disease
abstract: Comprehensive untargeted metabolomic analysis reveals altered circulating amino acid derivatives and secondary bile acids in patients following acute coronary syndrome, demonstrating the functional metabolic role of gut dysbiosis.

title: Akkermansia muciniphila and Vascular Endothelial Protection
abstract: Colonization by Akkermansia muciniphila strengthens intestinal tight junctions, inhibits metabolic endotoxemia, and protects vascular endothelial cell monolayers against inflammatory cytokine-mediated apoptosis in ApoE knockout mice.

title: Impact of Broad-Spectrum Antibiotics on Post-Infarction Myocardial Healing
abstract: Depletion of gut microbiota through broad-spectrum antibiotics impairs the immune response necessary for cardiac remodeling following myocardial infarction, resulting in increased left ventricular rupture and mortality.

title: Mediterranean Diet Modulation of Gut Taxa and Coronary Artery Calcium
abstract: Adherence to a polyphenol-rich Mediterranean dietary pattern induces enrichment of Roseburia and Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, correlating inversely with coronary artery calcium progression in high-risk asymptomatic adults.

title: Secondary Bile Acid Receptor TGR5 Signaling in Vascular Tone
abstract: Gut bacterial conversion of primary to secondary bile acids activates the G-protein bile acid receptor TGR5, eliciting vasodilation via nitric oxide-dependent signaling in resistance arteries.

title: Microbial Tryptophan Catabolites and Aryl Hydrocarbon Receptor Activation
abstract: Indole derivatives produced by gut commensals from dietary tryptophan bind the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR), preserving intestinal mucosal homeostasis and suppressing hypertensive renal and vascular end-organ injury.

title: Fecal Microbiota Transplantation in Metabolic Syndrome and Arterial Stiffness
abstract: A randomized double-blind controlled trial demonstrates that allogenic fecal microbiota transplantation from lean vegan donors significantly reduces pulse wave velocity and carotid-femoral arterial stiffness in obese metabolic syndrome patients.

title: Role of Gut-Derived MicroRNAs in Cardiac Hypertrophy
abstract: Extracellular vesicles originating from intestinal epithelial cells transport distinct non-coding microRNAs that modulate myocardial fibroblast activation and collagen cross-linking during sustained pressure overload.

title: Intermittent Fasting Induces Microbial Restructuring and Cardiometabolic Protection
abstract: Time-restricted feeding regimens reshape circadian oscillations of the gut microbiome, elevating circulating beta-hydroxybutyrate and decreasing systemic oxidative stress markers in hypertensive patients.

title: Bacterial Extracellular Vesicles as Novel Mediators of Atherogenesis
abstract: Outer membrane vesicles produced by intestinal Gram-negative bacteria infiltrate the arterial intima, accelerating macrophage foam cell formation and necrotic core expansion in vulnerable plaques.
